# 2 Samuel Chapter 20 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 192v–192r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_020_page_001.jpg, 2SA_020_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Now a worthless man happened to be there, whose name was Sheba the son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. He blew the trumpet and said, "We have no portion in David, and we have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents, O Israel!"

**2** So all the men of Israel withdrew from David and followed Sheba the son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed loyal to their king, from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

**3** David came to his house at Jerusalem. The king took the ten concubines whom he had left to keep the house and put them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but did not go in to them. They were shut up until the day of their death, living as if in widowhood.

**4** Then the king said to Amasa, "Call the men of Judah together to me within three days, and be here yourself."

**5** So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he delayed beyond the appointed time.

**6** David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord's servants and pursue him, lest he find fortified cities and escape from us."

**7** So there went out after him Joab's men, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men. They went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

**8** When they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Now Joab was wearing his military garment, and over it was a belt with a sword in its sheath fastened at his hip. As he stepped forward, the sword fell out.

**9** Joab said to Amasa, "Is it well with you, my brother?" And with his right hand Joab took Amasa by the beard to kiss him.

**10** But Amasa did not notice the sword in Joab's hand. Joab struck him with it in the belly, and his entrails poured out on the ground. He did not need to strike a second blow, and Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba the son of Bichri.

**11** One of Joab's young men stood beside the body and called out, "Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David — follow Joab!"

**12** But Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road. When the man saw that all the people stopped, he dragged Amasa from the road into a field and threw a garment over him, because everyone who came by stopped when they saw him.

**13** Once he was removed from the road, all the people went on after Joab to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

**14** Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel of Beth-maacah, and all the Bicrites assembled and followed him in.

**15** Joab's forces came and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maacah. They cast up a siege mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart. And all the troops were battering the wall to bring it down.

**16** Then a wise woman called from the city, "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab, 'Come here, that I may speak to you.'"

**17** He came near her, and the woman said, "Are you Joab?" He answered, "I am." Then she said, "Listen to the words of your servant." He answered, "I am listening."

**18** She said, "In the old days they used to say, 'Let them inquire at Abel,' and so they would settle a matter.

**19** I am one of the peaceable and faithful in Israel. You seek to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?"

**20** Joab answered, "Far be it from me, far be it, that I should swallow up or destroy!

**21** That is not the case. But a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted his hand against the king, against David. Give up him alone, and I will withdraw from the city." The woman said to Joab, "His head shall be thrown to you over the wall."

**22** Then the woman went to all the people in her wisdom. They cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. He blew the trumpet, and they dispersed from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.

**23** Now Joab was over all the army of Israel, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites.

**24** Adoram was over the forced labor, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was the recorder.

**25** Sheva was secretary, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests.

**26** And Ira the Jairite was also a priest to David.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators handle this compact narrative well: Sheba's revolt and rallying cry (vv.1–2), the concubines' fate (v.3), Amasa's delay and Joab's murder of him (vv.4–13), the siege of Abel Beth-maacah and the wise woman's negotiation (vv.14–22), and David's cabinet list (vv.23–26). The murder of Amasa (vv.8–10) is the chapter's most challenging passage, requiring careful attention to the ambiguous "and it fell" of v.8 and the gruesome detail of v.10. The wise woman's speech (vv.18–19) contains textual difficulties but all three translators capture its essential rhetoric: Abel is a city of counsel and peace, and destroying it would be to swallow up YHWH's inheritance.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.1 — "worthless man" vs. "troublemaker"
- **EMET:** "man of-worthlessness [beliyya'al]"
- **LOGOS:** "worthless man"
- **PNEUMA:** "troublemaker"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "worthless man." The Hebrew *ish beliyya'al* is a loaded deuteronomistic term meaning "man of worthlessness/wickedness." LOGOS preserves the theological weight; PNEUMA's "troublemaker" trivializes it.

---

### V.1 — "portion" vs. "stake"
- **EMET:** "portion [cheleq]"
- **LOGOS:** "portion"
- **PNEUMA:** "stake"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "portion." The Hebrew *cheleq* means portion/share and carries covenantal overtones of inheritance. PNEUMA's "stake" is modern and loses the resonance with land-inheritance language.

---

### V.2 — "stayed loyal" vs. "clung"
- **EMET:** "clung [davqu]"
- **LOGOS:** "stayed loyal"
- **PNEUMA:** "stayed loyal"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "stayed loyal." The Hebrew *davqu* means to cling/cleave (the same verb as Gen 2:24). Both LOGOS and PNEUMA capture the political sense; EMET's "clung" is more literal but slightly awkward in this context.

---

### V.3 — "living as if in widowhood" vs. "widowhood of living" vs. "like widows"
- **EMET:** "[in]-widowhood of-living [almanut chayyut]"
- **LOGOS:** "living as if in widowhood"
- **PNEUMA:** "like widows, for the rest of their lives"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "living as if in widowhood." LOGOS captures the oxymoronic Hebrew *almanut chayyut* (living widowhood) accurately. PNEUMA's paraphrase adds "for the rest of their lives" which, while true, is already stated ("until the day of their death").

---

### V.6 — "escape from us" vs. "tear out our eye" vs. "slip through our fingers"
- **EMET:** "tear-out our-eye [vehitstsil enenu]"
- **LOGOS:** "escape from us"
- **PNEUMA:** "slip through our fingers"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "escape from us." The Hebrew is notoriously difficult (*vehitstsil enenu*). LOGOS's "escape from us" captures the practical sense. PNEUMA's "slip through our fingers" is vivid but adds an idiom not in the Hebrew. EMET's literal "tear out our eye" preserves the MT but is opaque in English.

---

### V.8 — "the sword fell out" vs. "the sword slid out"
- **EMET:** "he-went-out and-it-fell [vayyippol]"
- **LOGOS:** "the sword fell out"
- **PNEUMA:** "the sword slid out"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the sword fell out." The Hebrew *vayyippol* means "it fell." LOGOS is precise; PNEUMA's "slid" implies a smooth, deliberate motion not in the verb.

---

### V.9 — "Is it well with you" vs. "How are you"
- **EMET:** "Is-it-peace [ha-shalom] [with]-you, my-brother?"
- **LOGOS:** "Is it well with you, my brother?"
- **PNEUMA:** "How are you, brother?"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Is it well with you, my brother?" LOGOS preserves the *ha-shalom* greeting that functions as bitter irony — the greeting of peace before a murder. PNEUMA's casual "How are you" flattens this.

---

### V.10 — "belly" vs. "belly"
- **EMET:** "to the-belly [el-ha-chomesh]"
- **LOGOS:** "in the belly"
- **PNEUMA:** "into his belly"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "in the belly." All three agree on the anatomical location. The Hebrew *chomesh* specifically refers to the fifth rib area/abdomen — Joab's signature strike point.

---

### V.12 — "wallowing" vs. "lying in a pool of blood"
- **EMET:** "rolling [mitgollel] in-the-blood"
- **LOGOS:** "lay wallowing in his blood"
- **PNEUMA:** "lying in a pool of blood"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "lay wallowing in his blood." The hitpael *mitgollel* means rolling/wallowing — implying Amasa was not yet fully dead and was writhing. LOGOS captures this; PNEUMA's "lying in a pool" suggests a static corpse.

---

### V.18 — "inquire at Abel" vs. "ask counsel at Abel" vs. "go ask at Abel"
- **EMET:** "Asking let-them-ask [sha'ol yish'alu] in-Avel"
- **LOGOS:** "Let them but ask counsel at Abel"
- **PNEUMA:** "Go ask at Abel"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Let them inquire at Abel." A compromise: "inquire" captures the formal sense of *sha'al* (to ask/seek counsel) while being more concise than LOGOS's rendering and more dignified than PNEUMA's.

---

### V.19 — "peaceable and faithful" vs. "peaceful and loyal"
- **EMET:** "peaceable [shelumey] [and]-faithful [emuney] of-Yisra'el"
- **LOGOS:** "peaceable and faithful in Israel"
- **PNEUMA:** "peaceful and loyal in Israel"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "peaceable and faithful in Israel." LOGOS's rendering preserves the Hebrew pair *shelumey emuney* with appropriate formal register. PNEUMA's "loyal" shifts the sense of *emunah* (faithfulness/trustworthiness) toward political allegiance.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
